terms.why: Keeps Héroe capitalised so it reads as the game's own noun, not a description.
Short, and 'entrar en la Zona' is how a commentator would say it.
Literal, and it stays a noun the player learns rather than a metaphor that drifts.
The moment a player becomes a hero. 'Despertar' carries the same one-off, irreversible sense.
'Entreno' is the everyday word; 'entrenamiento' is the formal one, and two characters too long for the labels that carry it.
'Tienda de Aficionados' is a translation; 'Tienda del Club' is what a ground actually calls it.
'Expectación' is correct but 11 characters, and it broke the copy budget on every label that carries it. 'Ambiente' is what a ground actually says about a club people are talking about.
Unlike Hero License or the Zone, this is a common noun in both languages — English writes it lowercase mid-sentence too, so Spanish must be allowed to. What is locked is the WORD, not its case.
